title: Give the approximate pKa
asks: A compound is drawn. Write its approximate pKa.

know.h: {{pKa}} = -log {{Ka}}. The lower the {{pKa}}, the stronger the acid. Each unit is a factor of ten.
The {{pKa}} of a compound is the {{pKa}} of its most acidic hydrogen. Be able to find that hydrogen: look at the functional groups, not the carbon chain.
Strong acids, all below zero: H-I -10, H-Br -9, H-Cl -8, {{H3O+}} -1.5, {{CF3CO2H}} -1.5.
About 10: phenol (O-H on a benzene ring) and {{H2S}}. A thiol R-SH and an ammonium ion {{RNH3+}} are about 10 to 11.
know.from: FA24 Exam 2, Q1A; Lecture 10/29, p. 3; pKa table

know.h: About 16: water 15.7 and alcohols. In solution: methanol 15.5, ethanol 15.9, isopropanol 16.5, tert-butanol 17.0.
25: a terminal alkyne, a hydrogen on a triple-bond carbon ({{sp}}, 50% s character).
38: the N-H of ammonia or a neutral amine.
50 to 60: an alkane C-H. The exam key accepts about 50 for pentane.

Estimate by analogy. The carbon skeleton hardly matters: cyclohexanol is an alcohol (16), 1-butyne a terminal alkyne (25), propanoic acid a carboxylic acid (4), p-cresol a phenol (10), diisopropylamine an amine (38), butane an alkane (50).

The amine trap. A neutral amine is drawn: the acid is its N-H, 38. The value of about 11 belongs to the ammonium ion, the amine's conjugate acid, and applies only when the nitrogen is drawn with a positive charge.

Be able to draw the conjugate base and say what stabilizes it: resonance for phenol and carboxylic acids, hybridization for the alkyne, size for S-H and H-X, induction for {{CF3CO2H}}. The reason lets you rebuild a number you have forgotten.
The lecture's numbers are the answers. Write {{H2S}} 10 (tables say 7), H-F 4 (tables 3.2), {{CF3CO2H}} -1.5 (tables about 0), amine N-H 38 (tables 36 to 38).

method: Read the drawing exactly: note every O-H, S-H, N-H and every charge.
List the kinds of hydrogen in the molecule and name the functional group each belongs to.

Pick the most acidic kind, in this order: {{CO2H}} (4), phenol O-H or S-H or a charged N-H (about 10), alcohol O-H (16), alkyne C-H on the triple bond (25), neutral N-H (38), any other C-H (50 to 60).
Write the ladder value for that group. Ignore extra alkyl groups and rings that are not attached to the acidic atom.
Adjust only for something the lecture taught: fluorines next to a {{CO2H}} (down to -1.5), a bulkier alcohol (up toward 17).
Check that the number makes sense by picturing the conjugate base and what stabilizes it.

pitfalls.h: Writing 11 for a neutral amine. That is the {{pKa}} of its conjugate acid. The neutral amine's N-H is 38.
Quoting the wrong hydrogen: the {{CH3}} of propyne (50) in place of the hydrogen on the triple bond (25), or the less acidic of two functional groups.
Writing 10 for any O-H near a ring. Only an O-H directly on a benzene ring is a phenol. Cyclohexanol is 16 and benzoic acid is 4.
Giving H-F a negative value like the other hydrogen halides. H-F is 4.
Copying the oxygen value onto sulfur: {{H2S}} and thiols are about 10, not 16.
Giving 25 to an alkyne with no hydrogen on the triple bond. Only a terminal alkyne has that hydrogen.
